why.text: Chalk, marl or sand slopes drain naturally, and a unique climate gives grapes a natural acidity ideal for sparkling wine.

styles.text: Sparkling only, white or rosé, made by second fermentation in the bottle; vintage or non-vintage.

climate.text: Northern vineyards with two influences: oceanic (regular rain, mild seasonal contrasts) and continental (sometimes destructive frosts, sunny summers).

soil.text: Hard limestone or chalk cuesta fronts; slopes of chalk, marl or sand. Chalk drains excess water and rehydrates the soil in dry weather.

tastes.text: Fresh acidity in all wines. Young: flowers, white fruit, citrus, mineral notes. Mature: yellow and cooked fruit, spice. Oldest: candied fruit, undergrowth, toast.

styles.name: Blanc de blancs
styles.text: White Champagne made only from white grapes.

styles.name: Blanc de noirs
styles.text: White Champagne made only from black grapes.

styles.name: Rosé
styles.text: Made by blending or by saignée (bleeding).

styles.name: Millésimé
styles.text: Vintage wine; at least 36 months ageing from bottling (15 for non-vintage).
